tasks.objective: Prepare source-shaped PMB records and assess provenance, definitions, experimental units, and unresolved gaps before fitting.

evidence.quote: The planned preparation step splits mixed source blocks into PK, PD, MIC, validation and benchmark inputs, then checks provenance, units, dose histories, experimental units and missing fields to identify usable records and unresolved gaps before fitting.

tasks.objective: Assess and fit eligible mouse, rat, and rabbit systemic PK models and pulmonary components where supported.

evidence.quote: The planned animal PK step selects eligible systemic and, where supported, pulmonary models for mouse, rat and rabbit, evaluating fit, parameter identifiability and held-out prediction where the design permits.

tasks.objective: Assess supported cross-species scaling, conduct the frozen held-out horse check, and produce prospective human PK predictions.

evidence.quote: The planned translation uses supported animal models, body size, protein binding and justified physiological relationships, comparing scaling with and without each species rather than assuming that more species is better. After mouse, rat and rabbit scaling is frozen, it predicts horse profiles under reported horse doses, compares them with held-out horse figures as an intermediate large-body-weight translation check, and records the result without retuning.

The project plans to predict human concentration-time profiles, AUC and Cmax with uncertainty under specified doses and routes, then freeze those predictions before opening human outcomes. The required doses and routes are unresolved in MI015.

tasks.objective: Assess eligible K. pneumoniae exposure-response records, compare the specified indices and regression families, and estimate only supported PD targets.

evidence.quote: For eligible K. pneumoniae data, the planned PD analysis compares fAUC/MIC, fCmax/MIC and fT>MIC using ordinary Emax and sigmoid Emax/Hill regression, estimates supported exposure targets, or reports that the data cannot determine a best index or target.

tasks.objective: Validate frozen human PK predictions against separately released actual dose histories and observed plasma PK, assessing ELF separately if compatible data exist.

evidence.quote: Human validation is planned by applying the frozen model to actual human dose histories, comparing predicted and observed plasma PK, assessing ELF separately when compatible data exist, and reporting bias, precision, exposure agreement and predictive uncertainty against criteria fixed before validation.

tasks.objective: After PK validation and PD qualification, assess per-MIC PTA and separate MIC-weighted attainment for prespecified human scenarios, with an exploratory efficacious-dose estimate only if supported.

evidence.quote: After PK validation and PD qualification, the planned PTA step simulates a prespecified human population and dosing scenarios, processes the MIC distribution, and includes an exploratory efficacious-dose estimate, uncertainty and the final published-result benchmark where supported. It delivers PTA tables or curves, a feasibility conclusion and reproducible code, or explains why PTA is not estimable if required inputs are missing. SC029 specifies the distinct attainment outputs.

requirements.description: Identify PMB source blocks and retain study and source identifiers, original units, dose histories, missingness, BLQ limits, provenance, and experimental-unit level. Distinguish original observations, digitized observations, and group summaries; do not infer individual trajectories or exposure-response joins.

evidence.quote: PMB_source_tables_by_species.xlsx is described as the single animal and in-vitro data workbook. Its sheets retain source-shaped tables and notes, not a ready-made modeling dataset.

Source identifiers, units, missing values and BLQ limits must be preserved. Group means and digitized observations are not individual animals; IDs, variability, exposure-response links and missing measurements must not be invented.

tasks.objective: Prepare traceable PK, PD, MIC and validation input definitions, preserving experimental units, biological distinctions and unresolved gaps.

evidence.quote: Planned data preparation splits mixed source blocks into PK, PD, MIC and validation inputs; checks provenance, units, dose histories, analytes, matrices, experimental units and missing fields; and identifies usable records and unresolved gaps before fitting.

tasks.objective: Define inputs for eligible animal systemic PK modeling and supported pulmonary or CSF components, retaining alternative parameter evidence at its actual evidence level.

evidence.quote: Planned animal PK work selects eligible systemic models for each species with usable data, evaluates fit and parameter identifiability, evaluates held-out prediction where design permits, and documents exclusion or exploratory use of summary-only, figure-only or radiolabel evidence. Component support is governed by SC031.

tasks.objective: Define inputs for animal-to-human translation and prospective human concentration-time, AUC, Cmax and fT>MIC predictions with uncertainty.

evidence.quote: Predict human concentration-time profiles, AUC, Cmax and fT>MIC with uncertainty under specified doses and infusion durations, then freeze the animal model, scaling and predictions. Access to human outcomes follows MI004; prediction conditions remain subject to MI007.

tasks.objective: Define matched inputs for comparing the three free-exposure indices using both regression families and estimating separate, supported PD targets.

evidence.quote: For eligible data, planned PK/PD analysis compares fT>MIC, fAUC/MIC and fCmax/MIC using ordinary Emax and sigmoid Emax/Hill regression separately by organism and infection site. Estimate supported exposure targets, or report that available data cannot determine a best index or target.

tasks.objective: Define the protected human reference inputs and prespecified criteria for independent validation of frozen human PK predictions.

evidence.quote: Planned human validation applies the frozen model to the doses and infusion conditions in SC026, compares predicted and observed plasma PK, and assesses other matrices separately when compatible data exist. Report bias, precision, exposure agreement and predictive uncertainty against criteria fixed before validation.

tasks.objective: Define inputs for per-MIC PTA, separate distribution-weighted attainment and a supported exploratory efficacious-dose estimate, culminating in a reproducible feasibility assessment.

evidence.quote: After PK validation and PD qualification, planned PTA simulation uses a prespecified human population and dosing scenarios, including infusion duration, to estimate attainment at each MIC. Process the MIC distribution and report distribution-weighted attainment separately. Include an exploratory efficacious-dose estimate where supported, with uncertainty; deliver PTA tables/curves, a feasibility conclusion and reproducible code. If required inputs are missing, report why PTA is not estimable.

requirements.description: Preserve the project drug, model-import restrictions and designated animal/in-vitro workbook role throughout all tasks.

evidence.quote: R01: Use meropenem as the sole test drug; comparators in the sources are not substitutes. Do not import the apramycin model or its parameters.

Meropenem_source_tables_by_species.xlsx is the single animal and in-vitro data workbook; its sheets retain source-shaped tables and notes rather than a ready-made modeling dataset. These are proposal-described resource roles, not findings from inspecting the workbook.

conditions: Applies across T01 through T06; source roles do not establish access, coverage or adequacy.

requirements.description: Retain source-level identity, measurements, units, censoring and experimental-unit meaning before any downstream preparation.

evidence.quote: Preserve source identifiers, units, missing values and detection limits. Group means, published fitted parameters and digitized points are not individual animals; flag means containing substituted detection-limit values. Do not invent IDs, variability—including interindividual variability from group summaries—exposure-response links or missing measurements.

conditions: Applies to all later input branches.

requirements.description: Define biological compatibility and preserve every distinction needed to assess a proposed conversion or physiological bridge.

evidence.quote: Keep routes; unchanged meropenem, H-4295 and total 14C; total versus unbound drug; and plasma, serum, whole blood, ELF, CSF, tissue fluid and tissue homogenate separate. Separate per-animal from per-kilogram parameters and neutropenic, renally impaired, septic, infected, pregnant and repeat-dose animals from healthy single-dose animals. In-vitro DHP-I kinetics are not PK. Every conversion or physiological bridge requires a recorded justification.

evidence.quote: R20: Report model feasibility as the primary outcome, without presenting it as a clinical dosing recommendation or proof of generalizability. A successful fit is not predictive validation, and human PK agreement does not validate antibacterial efficacy or safety. Preserve failures and data gaps.

After PK validation and PD qualification, planned PTA simulation uses a prespecified human population and dosing scenarios, including infusion duration, to estimate attainment at each MIC. Process the MIC distribution and report distribution-weighted attainment separately. Include an exploratory efficacious-dose estimate where supported, with uncertainty; deliver PTA tables/curves, a feasibility conclusion and reproducible code. If required inputs are missing, report why PTA is not estimable.

conditions: The primary outcome remains feasibility.

This requirements plan performs no analysis or scientific release.
